doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: First record solo, his own Bethlehem album, and Benny Goodman's call
summary: His first record solo was on Billy May's Bacchanalia in 1953, and Bethlehem gave him his only own album in 1955. Benny Goodman phoned to compliment it and hired him to sub on The Benny Goodman Story.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: That’s right. Some sophisticated changes that were demanding, yeah challenging is the word, that’s right. So that was fun. And a few things like that through the years don’t have a lot of record solo space. The first solo I played on a record was on a Billy May record called “Bacchanalia” and that was in 1953 I think. That was the first solo I played on a record. And then Ken Hanna was sort of in that period of time. And then Bethlehem hired me to do an album of my own in 1955 and that’s when they were still making ten inch LPs so that’s what it was. And that’s the only album I ever did on my own. And through that though, you might enjoy this story, we used to have a little joke thing we’d do when we’d be playing or something, get together playing with friends, just for fun, or

just hanging out or whatever. And the phone would ring and you’d say, “Oh maybe it’s Benny Goodman.” Well one time it was. And he complimented me on that album. He had heard it in New York. And he subsequently hired me to sub on the movie “The Benny Goodman Story” when they were making that movie, to replace Stan Getz. I didn’t have to solo, but to replace Stan Getz who had some court thing he had to appear at, or I don’t know what the details were. So I met him. And then around the same time I got a call from Woody Herman and that was something I always wanted to do. I had played in a lot of bands by then and that was the one band I really wanted to play on, because that was a tenor player’s band.
